AfterCardEnteredCombat.issue: Rollup of guard G2 per binding rule 4. The predicate and the effect match -- GhostSeed.cs:18-26 applies CardKeyword.Ethereal to any card CanAffect accepts -- but C#'s `CardCmd.ApplyKeyword` adds a keyword whose SOURCE is tracked (KeywordSources.Local), while the sim sets a single boolean `card.is_ethereal`, so the relic's contribution is indistinguishable from anyone else's (G2, dormant).

AfterRoomEntered.maps_to: on_combat_start (ghost_seed.py:27-30) -- the sim moves the sweep from the room-entry slot to the combat-start slot
AfterRoomEntered.issue: See guard G1. GhostSeed.cs:28-43 filters `room is CombatRoom` and then sweeps `Owner.PlayerCombatState.AllCards`; the sim iterates `self.player.all_cards` at on_combat_start. C#'s AfterRoomEntered for a combat room is dispatched at CombatRoom.cs:228, AFTER CombatManager.SetUpCombat but BEFORE StartCombatInternal's `AfterCreatureAdded` loop and `Hook.BeforeCombatStart` (CombatManager.cs:394-403) -- so the sim's sweep runs two dispatch points later. DORMANT (G1). The `room is CombatRoom` filter itself is faithful, including for event combats: EventModel.cs:625 builds a real CombatRoom, so an event fight qualifies on both sides.

guards.what: G1 (DORMANT): the sweep runs at BeforeCombatStart in the sim and at AfterRoomEntered in C#, two dispatch points earlier
guards.issue: MECHANISM: the C# order is SetUpCombat -> Hook.AfterRoomEntered (CombatRoom.cs:224-229) -> AfterCombatRoomLoaded -> StartCombatInternal, which runs `Hook.AfterCreatureAddedToCombat` for every starting creature and only then `Hook.BeforeCombatStart` (CombatManager.cs:380-403). The sim has no run-level slot a relic can use to reach into a combat -- RunState.enter_room dispatches after_room_entered before the combat is even constructed (run.py:981-983) -- so on_combat_start is the earliest available point, and it is the same slot audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json maps BeforeCombatStart onto. DORMANT: the only thing in the intervening window that could read Ethereal is an AfterCreatureAddedToCombat listener, and an executed census of the sim's Ethereal readers (`grep -rn is_ethereal sts2_rl/`) puts every consumer at TURN END -- combat.py:357 (the end-of-turn in-hand effects) and combat.py:370 (should_ethereal_trigger) -- with the only other writers being HexPower (powers.py:3210-3211) and relics/music_box.py:50. Nothing reads the flag between room entry and combat start on either side. Porting a monster or power whose AfterCreatureAddedToCombat reads card keywords makes it live; note that hook_dispatch gap G5 (MonsterModel is not a sim listener) would have to be fixed first for a monster to do it. Same shape as audit/records/relic/anchor.json N3 and audit/records/relic/girya.json G2, and recorded as a gap rather than a divergence for the same reason: the slot genuinely differs and the window is observable in principle.

guards.what: G2 (DORMANT): `!card.GetKeywordsWithSources(KeywordSources.Local).Contains(Ethereal)` (GhostSeed.cs:49) vs the sim's single `not card.is_ethereal` boolean
guards.issue: MECHANISM: C# tracks WHERE each keyword came from, and CanAffect only refuses a card that already has a LOCALLY sourced Ethereal -- a card that is Ethereal for some other reason still receives Ghost Seed's own local copy, so the two are independent and removing the other source leaves Ghost Seed's behind. The sim has one flag (cards/base.py:62) and ghost_seed.py:24 refuses any Ethereal card, so the relic's contribution is never recorded separately. DORMANT, with the concrete path named: HexPower (powers.py:3189-3238, applied by the ported Spectral Knight, monsters/glory/knights.py:119-120) sets `card.is_ethereal = True` after stashing `_hex_prev_ethereal`, and restores the stashed value when it is removed. So a Basic Strike or Defend that entered combat mid-fight while Hexed would be skipped by ghost_seed.py:32-34 (already ethereal) and then, on Hex removal, have Ethereal taken away -- where C#'s local keyword survives. What keeps it dormant is that Ghost Seed's own sweep runs at combat start, before any enemy can apply Hex, and Hex afflicts cards CREATED mid-combat, which are Status/Curse cards rather than Basic Strikes/Defends; making a Basic Strike enter combat while Hexed (a ported card-generation effect that creates a Basic card, or Hex applying to the whole hand) makes it live. The write direction is also worth noting: `card.is_ethereal = True` is permanent on the object, which is guard N2's subject.

guards.rationale: ghost_seed.py:21-25 is `card.rarity == CardRarity.BASIC and ('strike' in card.tags or 'defend' in card.tags)`, the same two clauses in the same order. Basic rarity plus the tag means the starting Strikes and Defends and any Basic copy generated later -- not Strike-tagged uncommons. Executed (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b06.py b06-misc`): a starting deck of 5 Strikes + 4 Defends comes out with all 9 Ethereal at combat start.

guards.what: N2 (SETTLED BY EXECUTION): `card.is_ethereal = True` is a permanent mutation of the card object, where CardCmd.ApplyKeyword adds a keyword to the COMBAT card model
guards.rationale: Binding rule 5: this is the kind of claim that must not rest on reading. Executed (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b06.py b06-misc`): with the relic in the run and the combat constructed the way RunState.create_combat does it -- `copy.deepcopy(self.deck)` (run.py:1136) -- 9 cards are Ethereal inside the combat and 0 in the run deck, matching C#. The probe also runs the counterfactual: a caller that passes the run deck WITHOUT copying leaves 9 Ethereal cards in the run deck permanently, outliving the relic. So the port is faithful because of an invariant that lives in run.py rather than in the relic; anyone changing create_combat's copy semantics breaks this relic silently. NOTE per binding rule 7: run.py and combat.py are not hashed by this record.

RelicModel.Flash() / FlashSfx / base.Status / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / InvokeDisplayAmountChanged / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / SelectionScreenPrompt / CardPreviewStyle / CardCmd.Preview / VfxCmd are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter, sfx and hover text, the card-screen prompt and layout, and vfx. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.

Both are every card in the combat regardless of pile -- hand, draw, discard, exhaust -- which is why the relic does not need an AfterCardDrawn hook to catch cards that arrive later from the draw pile. AfterCardEnteredCombat then covers only cards CREATED mid-combat, matching the sim's on_card_entered_combat docstring (hooks.py:402-404).
